## [open] chopTrees burns minutes on unreachable tall-canopy log segments — UngaBunga, 2026-09-01 09:42
Grove chop retest (post-ChopFix, count:4 maxDistance:32) SUCCEEDED overall (chopped:4, 17 oak_log
banked) — ChopFix confirmed working: budget no longer eaten by quarantine skips, ensureTool axe
craft + round-trip to grove both worked clean this run. But hit a distinct, separate cost: several
candidate trunk positions it tried were TALL oaks whose remaining upper log segments sit 4-8 blocks
above the last reachable foothold (e.g. target (4,99,71) with bot at y91, target (9,93,69) needing
y+2 with no stair/climb path, (7,96,68) needing y+5). Each one burned a full 3-attempt gotoLoopPf
cycle (~20-45s of real time, some finishing as false-reached instead of a clean immediate fail)
before chopTrees logged "could not reach/fell tree at X,Y,Z ... skipping N log position(s) of that
trunk" and moved on. 6 separate unreachable-segment failures logged this one run, costing a few real
minutes total, before it finally landed on 4 fully-reachable trees. Not fatal (task still completed,
matches the new "skip and continue, don't burn the whole task" behavior working as intended) but
worth a cheap pre-filter: before committing a gotoLoopPf attempt, check whether the target log
position is reachable via a plain vertical/short-hop path from current ground level (or already has
a stair/log-pillar the bot climbed for a lower segment of the same trunk) and skip straight to
"unreachable, next candidate" without the 3-attempt goto cycle for logs more than ~3 blocks above
the bot's own current foothold. Movements config already has allowParkour=false/no towers, so these
upper segments are genuinely unreachable without scaffolding — the fix is to recognize that FAST,
not to make them climbable.

## 2026-09-01 orchestrator self-report: force-fire before arrival (self-two-commanders)
Rescue staircase task-2 on Grog "done" in 1ms. NOT a bug: dig-law refusal, working as designed.
Two orchestrator errors stacked: (1) /staircase force:true fired while own /goto (task-1) still
running — force cancelled the positioning, bot never reached launch cell; (2) actual stand cell
z55 is outside rescue_ramp zone z56-58, columnEntersDigZone correctly said no.
LAW (now in REBUILD.md R1): goto → verify arrival via fresh /status position → THEN dig task.
force:true is for replacing a WRONG task, never for skipping the wait on your own right one.

1. **`sealStairCell`/`extendFloorTowards`/`isSolidGround` cave_air blindness** (skills.js) — dripstone caves read empty cells as `cave_air`/`void_air`, not `air`; the seal chain's narrow `name==='air'` checks false-read those as solid, breaking both the floor-extend rescue and the neighbor search. EAST scout leg, plain `/goto {x:132,y:101,z:52}` (pf, ~25-30 blocks from a known-good position at
x106/y89/z48). Two consecutive false-reaches with GROWING error each retry — "30.83 blocks
horiz/21.67 vert from goal" then "32.64h/30.77v" — meaning the bot was still actively falling
between the two failed-reach checks, not just off-target once. Health dropped **20→2** on the way
down (fall damage, not combat — no hostiles in range before or after). Landed in a `dripstone_caves`
pocket at y66 (from a y~89-101 starting band — a 25-35 block drop), skyLight 0.

Runner's panic reflex fired correctly on the health-2 tick and cancelled the task (that part
worked), but the recovery response itself had two real bugs, both worth fixing before the next
incident is less lucky:
1. `sealStairCell` logged "no solid neighbor found to seal" 3x and left the bot exposed on 2 of 4
   horizontal sides in a pitch-dark cave — an incomplete seal in exactly the scenario (dark,
   underground, post-fall) where a hostile spawn would matter most.
2. `emergencySeal`'s eat-fallback failed outright: `"emergencySeal: eat attempt failed: Item
   switched early to: undefined!\nItem: null"` — it didn't even manage to select a food item, let
   alone eat one, despite 2 bread sitting in inventory. This is the SAME bug family logged earlier
   this session (search "emergencySeal: eat attempt failed" above, the wheat_seeds mis-pick from a
   branchMine incident) but this manifestation is worse — not a wrong-item pick, a total failure to
   switch to ANY item. Two different failure modes off the same code path now confirmed in one
   session; the eat-item selection logic needs a real fix, not just a filter tweak.

Bot self-regenerated to full health before any further action was needed (food was full, helped
natural regen) and was bailed out via `/trigger home` immediately rather than pushing on from an
exposed position in the dark — no death, no item loss, but this was closer to a real death than
any other incident logged today. This is the THIRD `dripstone_caves` hit this session (see the two
entries above) but the first two were "just" pathfinder wedges; this one shows the false-reach bug
can turn dripstone_caves terrain into a real fall-damage/near-death hazard, not merely an
inconvenience. Reinforces the fix suggestion already on the branchMine false-reach entry above:
**`/goto`'s false-reach recovery needs a hard vertical-drop guard** — if a false-reach retry shows
a GROWING vertical gap (still falling) rather than a shrinking one, abort and reconfirm footing
before issuing another blind retry, instead of repeating the same failed movement into open air.

session — needs an actual edible-item filter (check `foodPoints`/`isFood`), not a second patch that
also doesn't fix it.

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	// =============================================================================
3	// baritone-runner.mjs — HTTP wrapper around a HeadlessMc + Baritone MC client.
4	//
5	// One node process per bot. Command wire = HMC launcher stdin.
6	// State wire  = the game client's own <gameDir>/logs/latest.log tail.
7	// NO RCON anywhere in this file. LAW.
8	//
9	// Launch recipe below is the FIELD-PROVEN one from cave/BARITONE.md
10	// ("Round 2 FINAL update — verdict: WORKS", 2026-09-01) as first proven by
11	// hmc-launch8.mjs. Do not "improve" the three load-bearing quirks:
12	//   1. NO  -lwjgl               -> the headless render stub hangs forever on
13	//                                  1.21.11 blur-pipeline uniforms. Real GPU +
14	//                                  hidden real window instead.
15	//   2. NO  --quickPlayMultiplayer -> silently never fires on this HMC/MC pair.
16	//                                  Join is driven manually by writing
17	//                                  `connect <host> <port>` to launcher stdin
18	//                                  once the title screen is up (~35 s).
19	//   3. YES -Dhmc.jline.enabled=false -> hmc-specifics spins a SECOND JLine
20	//                                  reader inside Minecraft.<init>; over a
21	//                                  plain (non-TTY) pipe it throws
22	//                                  IllegalStateException and kills the client.
23	//                                  The softer hmc.jline.dumb.* flags do NOT
24	//                                  fix this one.
25	// =============================================================================
26	//
27	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	// PINNED VERSIONS  — every artifact below is an explicit, on-disk, pinned file.
29	//                    NOTHING in this runner resolves a "latest" URL or tag.
30	//                    The runner never downloads: preflight() fails loudly if a
31	//                    pinned file is missing rather than fetching a replacement.
32	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	//   Java runtime      : 21.0.10   C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe
34	//   HeadlessMc launcher: 2.10.0   bots/<NAME>/headlessmc-launcher.jar
35	//                                 (sha-identical copy of
36	//                                  shared/headlessmc-launcher.jar)
37	//   Minecraft         : 1.21.11
38	//   Fabric loader     : 0.19.3    version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11`
39	//                                 installed under the SHARED mc install
40	//                                 (%APPDATA%\.minecraft\versions\...)
41	//   Fabric API mod    : 0.141.6+1.21.11
42	//                                 fabric-api-0.141.6+1.21.11.jar
43	//   Baritone          : 1.17.0    baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
44	//                                 (cabaletta official, built FOR 1.21.11)
45	//   hmc-specifics     : 2.4.0     hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar
46	//                                 (the version-stamped file HMC itself cached
47	//                                  under HeadlessMC/specifics/ — NOT the
48	//                                  "-latest" named download in shared/, which
49	//                                  would double-load as a second copy of the
50	//                                  same mod and crash fabric)
51	//
52	//   HMC_LAUNCH_TARGET below is the launcher's version selector. It is matched
53	//   against the installed version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11`, which is
54	//   the only fabric version installed — so it is unambiguous, not a "latest".
55	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	//
57	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	// PER-INSTANCE gameDir — how two bots are kept from colliding
59	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
60	// HeadlessMc 2.10.0 ignores the launcher process cwd when choosing the game
61	// directory: by default it passes `--gameDir %APPDATA%\.minecraft` to every
62	// client it spawns. Two bots would then share one logs/latest.log (the state
63	// wire), one baritone/settings.txt, one options.txt, one servers.dat.
64	//
65	// Mechanism found (by decompiling headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar):
66	//   LauncherProperties.GAME_DIR = config key `hmc.gamedir`
67	//     -> LauncherBuilder reads it, defaulting to the mc install dir, and
68	//        FileManager.mkdir()s it
69	//     -> ProcessFactory passes it to the child JVM as `--gameDir <path>`
70	//        and logs `Game will run in <path>` (our proof line).
71	//   Sibling key `hmc.game.dir.for.each.version` would append a per-version
72	//   subdir; pinned to false so the path is exactly what we set.
73	//
74	// It is a CONFIG-FILE key, not a `launch` flag (the launch command has no
75	// gamedir flag), and HMC's config.properties is resolved from the launcher's
76	// cwd — which IS per bot. So the isolation is:
77	//
78	//   bots/<NAME>/                        <- launcher cwd, per bot
79	//     headlessmc-launcher.jar
80	//     HeadlessMC/config.properties      <- carries hmc.gamedir + offline user
81	//     HeadlessMC/<uuid>/                <- per-bot extracted natives (already
82	//                                          isolated by cwd, HMC-side)
83	//     gamedir/                          <- hmc.gamedir target, per bot
84	//       mods/                           <- pinned mods, per bot
85	//       logs/latest.log                 <- STATE WIRE, per bot
86	//       baritone/settings.txt           <- safety config, per bot
87	//       options.txt, servers.dat, saves/, screenshots/ ...
88	//
89	// Shared (read-mostly, safe to share, big): the mc install at
90	// %APPDATA%\.minecraft — versions/, libraries/, assets/. Those are content-
91	// addressed downloads, not per-session state, so sharing them costs nothing
92	// and saves ~1 GB per extra bot.
93	//
94	// writeHmcConfig() rewrites config.properties on every boot, so hmc.gamedir
95	// can never drift back to the shared profile.
96	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

261	### Standing up a second bot
262	
263	```powershell
264	$n = 'BariBonk'   # <= 16 chars, stupid-funny naming law
265	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\$n"
266	Copy-Item C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared\headlessmc-launcher.jar "C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\$n\"
267	node baritone-runner.mjs --name $n --port 3302
268	```
269	
270	The runner creates `gamedir\mods\` and installs the pinned mods from `shared\`
271	itself. **Only run a second bot after checking the RAM budget in §5 — the law
272	is max 2 baritone clients alongside the 8-bot mineflayer fleet.**
273	
274	---
275	
276	## 4. Pinned versions
277	
278	Nothing in `baritone-runner.mjs` resolves a "latest" URL or tag, and the
279	runner never downloads. `preflight()` verifies every pinned artifact exists on
280	disk and **exits non-zero with a list** rather than fetching a substitute. It
281	also refuses to boot if the per-instance `mods\` contains any jar that is not
282	on the pinned list, which is what catches version drift.
283	
284	| component | version | file / path |
285	|---|---|---|
286	| Java | 21.0.10 | `C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe` |
287	| HeadlessMc launcher | 2.10.0 | `bots\<NAME>\headlessmc-launcher.jar` (copy of `shared\headlessmc-launcher.jar`) |
288	| Minecraft | 1.21.11 | `%APPDATA%\.minecraft\versions\1.21.11\` |
289	| Fabric loader | 0.19.3 | version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11` |
290	| Fabric API | 0.141.6+1.21.11 | `shared\fabric-api-0.141.6+1.21.11.jar` |
291	| Baritone | 1.17.0 | `shared\baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar` (cabaletta official, built for 1.21.11) |
292	| hmc-specifics | 2.4.0 | `shared\hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar` |
293	
294	Launcher version selector is `fabric:1.21.11`, which HMC matches against the
295	installed version id `fabric-loader-0.19.3-1.21.11`. That is the only fabric
296	version installed, so the selector is unambiguous — not a floating "latest".
297	
298	**Do not use `shared\hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar`.** It is the
299	same bytes but under the upstream "-latest" download name. HMC itself installs
300	the version-stamped `hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar` into
301	`<gamedir>\mods\`; having both names present makes Fabric abort with a
302	duplicate-mod error. The `-latest` copy is kept only as the original download
303	receipt. `preflight()` will refuse to boot if it ever lands in a mods dir.
304	
305	---

file.content:
## 1. Launch

```powershell
cd C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter
node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 --host localhost --mcport 25565
```

| flag | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` | `BariBrute` | bot name; also the offline MC username, the `bots\<NAME>\` dir, and the pid file. Hard-capped at 16 chars (MC username limit) — the runner exits if longer. |
| `--port` | `3301` | HTTP control port, bound to `127.0.0.1` only. Baritone heavy-lifters own 3301-3309. |
| `--host` | `localhost` | MC server host |
| `--mcport` | `25565` | MC server port |
| `--show-window` | off | leave the real GLFW window visible (debug only; default hides it) |

Boot timeline (all of it automatic):

```
t+0.0s   write bots/<NAME>/HeadlessMC/config.properties  (hmc.gamedir etc.)
t+0.0s   preflight: verify java, launcher jar, fabric version, pinned mods
t+0.0s   write <gamedir>/baritone/settings.txt  (safety block)
t+0.0s   delete stale <gamedir>/logs/latest.log, snapshot pre-existing java PIDs
t+0.0s   spawn  java -jar headlessmc-launcher.jar   (cwd = bots/<NAME>)
t+4.0s   stdin: launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Dhmc.jline.enabled=false"
t+39.0s  stdin: connect localhost 25565
t+51.0s  msg #set chatDebug true ; start position poll
```

Ready when `GET /status` returns `"phase":"in-world"` and a non-null
`position`. Typical wall time from launch to first position: **~55 s**.

### The three load-bearing quirks — do not "fix" them

1. **No `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's LWJGL redirection layer is incomplete for
   1.21.11's RenderPipeline, and the client hangs forever right after the
   `minecraft:blur/0` … `blur/5` uniform warnings. We run real LWJGL on the
   real GPU and hide the window instead.
2. **No `--quickPlayMultiplayer`.** It silently never fires on this HMC/MC
   pair — the client sits at the title screen forever with no log trace. The
   join is driven manually: after ~35 s, write `connect <host> <port>` to the
   launcher's stdin. (`hmc-specifics` `ConnectCommand` reads `args[1]` = host,
   `args[2]` = port; a raw space-separated line, no flags.)
3. **`-Dhmc.jline.enabled=false` on the CHILD JVM.** `hmc-specifics` mixes
   into `Minecraft.<init>` and starts a *second* JLine reader inside the game
   process; over the wrapper's plain (non-TTY) pipe it throws
   `IllegalStateException: Failed to start JLineCommandLineReader` and kills
   the client. The softer `hmc.jline.dumb*` flags do **not** fix this one, and
   `config.properties` does not reach the child JVM — it must be on `--jvm`.

Never add `-commands`: it conflicts with `hmc-specifics` (maintainer guidance,
headlessmc issue #390). `hmc-specifics` alone is the console surface.

---

BariOok launched and verified. All 3 checks done:

1. **RCON list**: confirms BariOok online server-side (real connection, not just wrapper self-report).
2. **/status (3303)**: connected:true, phase:in-world, sane.
3. **Smoke test**: goto+stop, real move (not "few blocks" — explain below), ground-truthed via RCON `data get entity BariOok Pos`/`Health` (independent of the wrapper, since no mineflayer bot was near enough to ground-truth via blockAt). Result: SUCCESS, health 20/20, no incident.

**Wrinkle worth knowing**: BariOok's login position was (-2,115,-4) — INSIDE the FEL no-go box (z=-4 well within the -16..24 range). Wrapper's own watchdog correctly caught it (`aborted:"nogo"`, auto #stop, zero damage) — safety layer worked exactly as designed. Since /goto refuses any target still inside the box, the smoke test HAD to be a real ~16-block move to actually clear it (couldn't do a token "few blocks" test without violating the no-go check) — went to (-2,115,-20), just outside. Confirmed via RCON: BariOok is now at (-1.48, 112, -19.7), safely outside, full health.

**Real finding, flagging clearly**: mid-task, /status showed stale position + `lastBaritoneLine:"No path found =("` for a good stretch — looked like a failure. RCON ground-truth proved the move had ACTUALLY SUCCEEDED already; /status just doesn't refresh position during an active task except via chatDebug path-line parsing, which apparently didn't catch this particular path's lines. Position field self-corrected the moment I sent /stop and the idle #goal poll resumed. Same "never trust the resolved status alone" lesson as pf/ash's own false-reach bugs — except backwards here (false FAILURE, not false success). Worth a note in BARITONE-RUNNER.md (didn't edit myself, not sure if that's your doc or BariBrute driver's to own) — recommend: during an active task, treat /status position as unreliable, cross-check via RCON or wait for idle before trusting it.

**Side note, not urgent**: port 3205 (Thak mineflayer) isn't responding right now — dropped off the RCON player list between my two `list` checks (13->12 players, Thak gone). Might already be your/his driver's planned stop for the cluster-3 finish, flagging in case it's not.

309	non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
310	bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking

312	and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
313	abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
314	(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
315	come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).

323	  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).

325	  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
326	  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
327	- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
328	  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
329	  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
330	- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
331	  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)

333	- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag

### Blocker 1 — `-lwjgl` render hang on blur uniforms

Root cause, near-certain: the exact string "Found unknown and unsupported
uniform" is **vanilla Mojang code**, not a headlessmc string — confirmed by
grepping public 1.21.11 decompile mirrors, it lives in
`com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlProgram`. On a real GPU this line is a harmless,
non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking
to a real GPU (`headlessmc-lwjgl/.../redirections/LwjglRedirections.java`),
and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).

Evidence the maintainers are actively chasing this exact surface, release by
release:
- **2.9.0** (2026-04-04): [PR #407](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/407)
  "fix(1.21.11): Fix crash" — fixed `MemoryUtil;memSlice`, which had literally
  been stubbed to always `return null` ("TODO... null is fairly safe rn"),
  causing the 1.21.11 boot NPE in
  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).
  Sibling [PR #406](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/406) fixed
  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)
  (unimined tooling), closed 2026-04-04 — separate from the runtime bugs above.
- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag
  are chore-only (logo, CI) — nothing queued that would fix this.
- Exhaustive search (issues/PRs/commits/discussions/code-search, org-wide) for
  "blur" or "uniform" turns up **nothing** else — the only unrelated hit is
  `hmc.lwjgl.uniformoffsetalignment` (`GL_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`,
  a buffer-alignment constant, not the blur pipeline's uniform names). **This
  exact hang is unreported upstream as of 2.10.0 / today.**
- No LwjglProperties flag exists to selectively skip RenderPipeline/uniform
  validation while staying in `-lwjgl` mode. `hmc.lwjgl.ignore.classes`
  exists but excluding a class from redirection while headless just crashes
  it against a real GL call with no context — not a usable escape hatch.

**Workaround that should fix it today: stop using `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's
own README says outright: "You can also achieve headless mode without
patching lwjgl by running headlessmc with a virtual framebuffer like Xvfb."
More to the point for us: BariBrute's host is a normal Windows desktop with a
real GPU and display, not a headless VM — there is no rendering gap to paper
over in the first place. Launching fabric 1.21.11 *without* `-lwjgl` uses
real, unpatched LWJGL against the real GPU driver, so the blur-uniform WARN
gets handled exactly as on any normal player client (logged once, harmless,
game keeps rendering) because it never touches headlessmc's incomplete
redirection layer at all.

# Sponge schematic v3 → v2 fix (Baritone can't load v3)

**Symptom:** a `.schem` file dropped in `cave/schematics/` builds fine in
WorldEdit/whatever exported it, but the pinned fleet Baritone jar
(`baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0`, tag v1.17.0, MC 1.21.11) throws
`UnsupportedOperationException: Unsupported Version of a Sponge Schematic`
when `#build` tries to load it.

**Root cause (field-checked against real cabaletta/baritone v1.17.0 source,
2026-09-01):** `SpongeSchematic.java` only accepts NBT root `Version` 1 or 2.
Every modern schematic tool exports **Sponge Schematic v3** by default. v3
also restructures the file — v1/v2 keep `Width/Height/Length/Palette/
BlockData` at the NBT root; v3 nests everything under a root `Schematic`
compound and further nests `Palette`/`Data` (renamed from `BlockData`) inside
a `Blocks` compound. So a v3 file isn't just version-flagged wrong, its
fields are literally not where Baritone's parser looks.

**Confirmed against real files:** all 4 schematics first dropped into
`cave/schematics/` for the hilltop-house project (`sites_classic-village-
house`, `sites_cozy-cabin`, `sites_rustic-farmhouse`, `github_samurai-house`)
were v3 and would have failed this way.

**Fix:** run the converter already in the repo —

```
node cave/schematics/convert-v3-to-v2.mjs cave/schematics/<name>.schem [more...]
```

It hoists the v3 fields back to v2's flat shape, stamps `Version=2`, writes
the fix **in place under the same filename** (so `/build {schematic:
"<name>"}` on the baritone wrapper just works with no caller-side change),
and preserves the untouched original alongside as `<name>.v3-original.schem`.
Round-trip-verifies (palette count + BlockData byte length unchanged) before
writing; running it again on an already-v2 file is a safe no-op.

**When to reach for this:** any time a new `.schem` lands in
`cave/schematics/` — check it before wiring a `/build` call, since the
failure mode is silent right up until baritone actually tries to build.

**Not touched by the fix (known limitation, not a bug):** Baritone's
`StaticSchematic` is block-states-only — it never reads `BlockEntities` (chest
contents, sign text, etc.), `Offset`, or `Metadata`, v3 or v2. A converted
schematic builds the block shell correctly; anything that needed NBT data
inside a container/sign will come out empty either way.

/BUILD ENDPOINT — SHIPPED (baritone-runner.mjs, Windows side, not in git repo):
- POST /build {schematic,x,y,z} -> deploy step copies cave/schematics/<name>.schem from WSL repo into <gameDir>/schematics/ (exact dir BuildCommand.java resolves against — field-checked real source), THEN msg #build <name> x y z. No-go gate on origin same as /goto (403 if inside box). Name sanitized (no path traversal).
- Cross-boundary copy uses \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-24.04\... UNC path (verified reachable from Windows PowerShell). Dry-ran the EXACT resolve+copy logic on the Windows side for real (not simulated) against 3 real repo files -> SHA256 hash match on every copy, extension auto-try (.schem then .schematic) works.
- #pause/#resume/#stop: already reachable, no code needed — /console whitelist already had #pause/#resume, /stop already its own endpoint.
- node --check clean on the edited wrapper.

RESEARCH VERDICT (builder settings, pinned baritone v1.17.0==1.21.11 branch, pulled+read the REAL cabaletta source, not guessed):
- allowInventory, buildInLayers, layerOrder, buildIgnoreBlocks, buildSubstitutes, okIfAir — ALL EXIST, confirmed in Settings.java.
- SET allowInventory=true in settings.txt (was implicit false). Load-bearing: default false means BuilderProcess only searches the 9 HOTBAR slots for material — restock protocol #4 (bots throw stacks at builder's feet -> full 36-slot inventory) would silently stall on "Missing materials" without this.
- buildInLayers/layerOrder left at safe defaults (off / bottom-to-top) — fine for a house, no overhangs need special handling that me can see.
- Sponge .schem support confirmed real (SpongeSchematic.java exists, parses via NBT).

CRITICAL FINDING (verified against the ACTUAL house-pick files, not theory): pinned baritone ONLY accepts Sponge Schematic Version 1 or 2 — v3 (modern WorldEdit default export, ALSO restructures the whole file under a nested "Schematic"+"Blocks" tag) hits an UnsupportedOperationException at #build time. ALL 4 real .schem candidates dropped in cave/schematics/ so far (village-house, cozy-cabin, rustic-farmhouse, samurai-house) WERE v3 — would have hard-failed on first #build attempt.
FIXED: wrote cave/schematics/convert-v3-to-v2.mjs (permanent, idempotent, round-trip-verifies palette+blockdata byte-for-byte before writing). Ran it — all 4 now fixed IN PLACE under their same canonical name (so /build {schematic:"name"} just works), original v3 bytes kept alongside as *.v3-original.schem for provenance. github_v2_house.schem was already native v2, untouched. A 6th file just landed too (github_rustic-cabin-9383.schematic, MCEdit format not sponge) — checked its real field names against baritone's MCEditSchematic.java parser, matches clean, no fix needed for that one.
Wrote a project skill (.claude/skills/sponge-schematic-v3-fix) so this doesn't get re-discovered blind next time — heads up though, .claude/ is gitignored by this repo's own policy so it's local-disk-only, not tracked, still works for skill discovery on this machine.

Standing by — restock-protocol wiring (mineflayer throw-at-feet) is #4 on your list and not something the wrapper needs changes for per your spec, so nothing pending on my end unless you want a live /build smoke test run.

+// Fix: target THIS bot's own process tree directly (launcher pid + its
+// direct java/javaw child), not "guess by exclusion". No staleness possible.
function killTree(cb) {
const pid = child?.pid;
-  const known = new Set(preexistingJavaPids);
-  const skip = [...known].join(',') || '0';
+  try { if (pid) process.kill(pid); } catch {}
+  if (!pid) { cb && cb(); return; }
const ps = `

-  "killing pid=$($_.Id)"

-  try { if (pid) process.kill(pid); } catch {}
execFile('powershell.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command', ps], (e, out) => {

cb && cb();

input.message:
TASK 2+3 — code complete, wrapper file (all in baritone-runner.mjs):

2. /setting endpoint (chose this over cramming into /console's whitelist, since #console's SAFE_CONSOLE_CHAT is exact-string zero-arg matching — #set always takes name+value, doesn't fit that shape safely):
   POST /setting {key, value} -> #set <key> <value>. Allowlist SETTABLE_KEYS = legitMine, allowInventory, chatDebug, allowDownward (bool-only v1, matches exactly what writeBaritoneSettings() already manages at boot — not opening arbitrary #set). 403 on non-whitelisted key, 400 on non-boolean value. This unblocks BariBruteDriver's earlier 403'd live-flip attempt. Live flip does NOT persist to settings.txt (file always gets fully rewritten from the fixed template at next boot anyway — same as chatDebug's existing boot-time #set, consistent with current design).

3. Goal-echo-as-position bug — FIXED. Root cause confirmed matches your ground-truth exactly: startPosPoll() only arms posPollPending while idle, but the reply is async — if a real task (/goto etc) starts in that ~0-4s window before the poll's own reply lands, Baritone's goal-set ACK for the NEW task ("Goal: GoalBlock{x=DEST}") is shape-identical to the idle poll's "here's your current position" echo, and posPollPending was still sitting armed, so it got consumed as if it were real position. Fix: a GoalBlock echo is now ONLY trusted as a position sample when state.task is null (nothing running) — otherwise logged+dropped, never guessed. Same family as the earlier stale-position finding, per your read — didn't touch that separate one (chatDebug simply not refreshing fast/often during active travel — different root cause, real fix would be periodic #eta-style polls during tasks too, flagging as a possible follow-up, not done).

VERIFIED via isolated simulation (copied the exact patched regex+state logic into a standalone harness, not guessed): (a) the exact race from your bug report — poll armed, task starts, only the destination echo arrives — now correctly produces NO false position instead of the wrong one; (b) legit idle #goal-poll reads still work unchanged; (c) real chatDebug position samples mid-task still work unchanged. All 3 pass.

node --check clean.

NOT YET LIVE — didn't relaunch to deploy this round. All 3 bots are mid-active-task under driver control right now (Brute #mine, Thak goto, Ook goto) and given task 1's relaunch just cost a real incident, didn't want to unilaterally interrupt them again back-to-back without you knowing. Say the word (or tell me to just go) and me relaunches all 3 (sequential, confirmed boot-by-boot, same safe pattern as the recovery) to get 2+3 live — should be clean now that killTree is fixed.

Reported. Summary of this round of work:

**Task 1 (relaunch BariBrute)** — done, but surfaced and fixed a serious live bug in the process: the old `killTree()` killed sibling bots as collateral (stale exclusion-snapshot logic broke the moment a second/third bot existed). This actually fired twice mid-recovery, taking down all 3 bots at one point. Root-caused via log-tail evidence, fixed with parent-child process targeting, then did a clean sequential recovery of all 3 bots — verified stable under real concurrency (Brute mining, Thak/Ook on active gotos, no more collateral).

**Task 2 (`/setting` endpoint)** — added, allowlisted to 4 boolean settings, unblocks the live-flip that was 403ing before.

**Task 3 (goal-echo-as-position bug)** — root-caused exactly per team-lead's ground-truth, fixed with a `state.task` guard, verified via an isolated simulation harness (3/3 scenarios pass, no regressions).

Held off on relaunching to deploy 2+3 since all 3 bots are mid-task under live driver control and just went through one disruption — flagged for team-lead's go-ahead rather than repeating the interruption unilaterally.

input.message:
CRASH DIAGNOSIS — plus a status correction first:

CURRENT LIVE STATE (just ground-truthed, all 3 ports): all 3 bari bots are UP and CONNECTED right now — BariBrute mining coal (uptime ~8min, stable since my earlier full recovery), BariThak mining iron, BariOok actively on the recon goto toward the chief-mission target (252,94,131). Log timestamps confirm BariBrute has run continuously since my recovery relaunch with zero further deaths — so whatever additional Ook/Brute cycling you saw must have already gotten resolved (by a driver or auto-recovery) before I got to checking. Nobody's waiting on a go from me right now — flag if that's wrong on your end.

ROOT CAUSE — NOT classic JVM heap-OOM. Ruled that out concretely:
- -Xmx3G IS correctly applied on all 3 live client JVMs (checked real command lines, not just source — confirmed pass-through works).
- ZERO hs_err_pid*.log crash dumps anywhere in any bot's directory (searched all 3 + shared root). A heap-OOM abort virtually always drops one of these — their total absence across 3 separate deaths points AWAY from "Java heap exhausted" and toward something killing the process from OUTSIDE the JVM (no graceful trace, no exception, log just stops).

REAL FINDING — your instinct about host RAM pressure was right, but the mechanism is more specific than "3 JVMs + server": 
- /mnt/c/Users/phili/.wslconfig has `memory=32GB` — WSL2 is explicitly configured to claim UP TO 32GB of the 47.2GB host.
- Real WSL-side usage right now (`free -h` inside WSL): only 7.4GB actually used out of that 31GB allowance, 21GB genuinely free on the Linux side.
- But Windows host shows only 14.2GB free system-wide right now — meaning vmmem is very plausibly sitting on a big chunk of that 32GB cap it doesn't currently need (WSL2's dynamic memory give-back to the host is known to be sluggish/incomplete without extra tuning), starving the Windows side.
- Windows-side ceiling: 3× baritone Xmx3G (9GB) + MC server Xmx6G (6GB) = 15GB of POSSIBLE peak heap demand crammed into a ~14GB free pool. A transient spike like BariBrute's 13.5M-movements/4s pathfind burst is exactly the kind of moment that could tip it over — and Windows' own low-memory process reclaim (not a Linux OOM-killer, but real) wouldn't leave a JVM crash trace, which matches what we see.

TWO fixes, different blast radius — did NOT execute either, both need your/chief's call:
1. (Best target, but disruptive) Lower .wslconfig memory cap, e.g. 32GB -> 12-16GB (real usage is only 7.4GB) to give Windows-side real headroom back. Requires `wsl --shutdown` + restart — that KILLS this entire WSL session (me included, everything cavecrew-side) mid-flight, so this is not mine to just run. Chief/Phili call, probably a deliberate maintenance-window action.
2. (Lower-risk, mine to do if you want) Drop each bot's -Xmx from 3G to something smaller (e.g. 2G) in baritone-runner.mjs JVM_ARGS — shrinks worst-case ceiling 9GB->6GB, one-line change, no WSL touch. Tradeoff: less heap headroom for genuinely big pathfinds (like that 13.5M-node burst) could itself trigger more GC pressure or a real heap-OOM later. Your call — say go and I'll do it + relaunch.

Given current state is stable and nothing's actively down, treating this as diagnosed-not-yet-fixed rather than urgent. Moving on to /toss research next, and will hold the /build smoke-test + the code-2+3 relaunch until you weigh in on the Xmx question (no point relaunching twice).

input.summary: /toss research: found a real path via hmc-specifics key+click+menu
input.message:
/TOSS RESEARCH — good news, there IS a real path. Not guessing, pulled the actual pinned source (Baritone v1.17.0 AND hmc-specifics 2.4.0, both exact-tag-matched to our jars).

BARITONE SIDE: confirmed zero drop/toss capability. Pulled DefaultCommands.java's full command list (30 commands) — PickupCommand exists (picks UP dropped items into inventory) but nothing for the reverse. BariBruteDriver's finding is airtight, not worth chasing further there.

HMC-SPECIFICS SIDE: it DOES have the building blocks, routed through the same raw stdin console channel we already use for connect/msg (not baritone's chat interception):
- `key <name> [--duration ms] [-release]` — presses/releases ANY keyboard key by name (real KeyCommand.java, in-game injection via HmcKeyboard, or an AWT-Robot OS-level mode via -robot). This can literally press Q (vanilla single-item drop) or Ctrl+Q (full-stack drop) on the CURRENTLY SELECTED HOTBAR slot, and digit keys 1-9 to select which hotbar slot first — no GUI needed at all for hotbar contents.
- `menu -inventory` — opens the real inventory screen (36 slots).
- `gui` — dumps the CURRENTLY OPEN screen's elements with real x/y/w/h/id (so slot coordinates are discoverable live, not guessed).
- `click <id|p> [x y] [button]` — clicks a specific gui element by id, or raw pixel coords + mouse button.
- `close` — closes the current screen cleanly.

PROPOSED v1 DESIGN (not built yet):
Simple case (covers most of it): for hotbar slots 1-9, `key <N>` to select + `key q --duration X` (or a Ctrl-held variant for full stack) to drop, small delay between each — zero GUI needed, lowest risk.
Full case (all 36 slots): `menu -inventory` -> `gui` to confirm slot layout -> for each occupied slot, `click <id> 0` (pick up stack onto cursor) -> `click p <x> <y> 0` at a point OUTSIDE the inventory panel bounds (vanilla's "drag out the window and release" = drop full stack) -> `close` when done.

WHY NOT BUILDING IT RIGHT NOW: this touches all 3 bots' real inventories and the exact click/coordinate/timing sequence genuinely needs live verification against a real running client before it's a wrapper endpoint anyone trusts — same "ground truth before shipping" standard as everything else this session. Recommend: let me do one live, careful experiment on an IDLE bot with a known test item (few cheap blocks, not real mined loot) to nail down the exact working sequence, THEN wire /toss for real. Say go and I'll do that next, or tell me priority vs the other open items (2+3 relaunch, /build smoke test, Xmx question).

Interim (c) — loot banked-in-transit in bot inventory — stays fine as the fallback until this lands.

All caught up and holding at a clean checkpoint. Status:

**Stable now:** all 3 bari bots up, connected, real tasks running (Brute mining coal, Thak mining iron, Ook on the chief recon mission). Wrapper file syntax-valid, fixes intact.

**Diagnosed & reported:** the JVM-death wave wasn't classic heap-OOM (ruled out: `-Xmx3G` confirmed applied, zero crash dumps anywhere). Real culprit: `.wslconfig` reserves 32GB for WSL while only using 7.4GB, squeezing Windows-side headroom to ~14GB against a ~15GB combined Baritone+MC-server heap ceiling. Flagged two fixes (WSL config retune vs. lower per-bot `-Xmx`), didn't execute either — both are team-lead/chief calls given the blast radius.

**Researched:** `/toss` — confirmed Baritone has zero drop capability, but hmc-specifics' real `key`/`menu`/`gui`/`click`/`close` commands give a concrete, buildable path (hotbar-key-drop for the simple case, full GUI click-sequence for all 36 slots). Proposed a live-experiment-first plan rather than shipping blind.

**Holding on team-lead's word for:** the Xmx tradeoff decision, the relaunch to deploy `/build`+`/setting`+the goal-echo fix (held back to avoid a third live disruption), the `/build` mini-schematic smoke test, and go-ahead on the `/toss` live experiment. Sent three detailed reports this round; standing by rather than pushing further unprompted on anything that touches the live bots again.

input.message:
BARITHAK BUNDLE COMPLETE. BariThak idle, HP 20/20, safe, ready for ThakDriver.

1. RELAUNCH — clean, RCON-verified, Brute/Ook untouched (zero collateral, killTree fix holding under real concurrency again). Live now: 2+3 code, Issue #9 work-zone watchdog, #pickup whitelisted. settings.txt: allowInventory true present; legitMine line missing again (same transient concurrent-edit-window gap as before — Baritone's compiled default is false so live behavior is still correct, not forcing a 3rd relaunch for cosmetics per your standing ruling).

2. /TOSS EXPERIMENT — full success, sequence+timing NAILED with real evidence (RCON before/after on BariThak's actual inventory, not guessed):
   - Added a scoped /native endpoint (key/menu/gui/click/close passthrough, separate whitelist from /console since these are hmc-specifics' own raw commands, not baritone chat) — needed this to even run the experiment, one extra quick relaunch to load it, included.
   - `key <N>` (1-indexed) selects hotbar slot N-1, confirmed exact.
   - `key q` alone = single-item drop. CONFIRMED: dripstone 3->2, real dropped entity ground-truthed (OnGround:1, Thrower=BariThak).
   - Full-stack drop = hold Ctrl + Q + release. CONFIRMED on dirt: 6->0 (whole stack gone, not decremented). BUT: first attempt with commands fired back-to-back (no delay) silently degraded to a single-item drop — the modifier hold needs to actually register before Q fires. Real, working recipe: `key left.control -indefinite` -> WAIT (~1-2s tested reliable, exact minimum untested) -> `key q` -> `key left.control -release`. This is the concrete timing spec for wiring /toss v1.
   - v1 design confirmed buildable: for each hotbar slot 1-9, select + ctrl-hold+delay+q+release, small gap between slots. Ready to wire whenever you want it as its own endpoint.

3. /BUILD SMOKE — partial result, honest report not a forced "clean pass": deployed test_pad_3x3.schem (my own tiny 3x1x3 cobblestone Sponge v2, built+round-trip-verified same way as the house schematics) to (25,90,65) near staging. Log confirms the CRITICAL thing: "Successfully loaded schematic for building" — the v3->v2 conversion fix is proven end-to-end in production, not just in my earlier isolated verification. Origin set correctly, builder engaged, composite goal shrank 8->6 targets (real progress). Then stalled — position + lastBaritoneLine both went static for 3+ min, zero cobblestone ever placed (checked all 9 cells via RCON execute-if). No error, no crash, just stuck on this specific spot's terrain during the pre-build clearing phase (couldn't identify the exact obstructing block via RCON guessing, didn't want to burn more of BariThak's window on it). Stopped cleanly, zero damage. Verdict: pipeline works, this test LOCATION didn't cooperate — recommend either a cleaner test_yard spot (open flat area, none currently defined anywhere I could find — BASE.md has no test_yard entry) or just trusting the schematic-load proof as sufficient and moving straight to the real house build with a driver watching.

Test schematic + deploy dir left in place, harmless. Standing by for next bot's window (Brute's salvage run) or further direction.

input.message:
BUNDLE #2 (BariBrute) — clean. Relaunch verified (RCON, siblings untouched), settings.txt fully correct this time (legitMine false present, no gap). Idle, safe, back at staging.

LEGITMINE-GAP INVESTIGATION: checked — writeBaritoneSettings() itself has zero branching/conditionals, it's one synchronous fs.writeFileSync with a fixed literal array, `legitMine false` is unconditionally line 1 every single call. There is NO internal code path that can omit it. Conclusion: not a bug in the function — it's an external race, this file lives outside git with (evidently) more than one of us editing it concurrently, and if a freshly-spawned wrapper's ES-module import reads the file mid-external-edit, THAT process's in-memory code is stale for its whole lifetime (self-corrects only on its own next full relaunch, matches what we've seen both times). No code fix available on my end — it's a process/tooling gap, not urgent per your call.

/TOSS V1 — shipped, but I want to give you the real result, not a polished one:
- Wired POST /toss: fixed hotbar sweep, your timing spec, refuses to start over another active task.
- Control-flow verified via isolated simulation first (busy-guard, mid-run cancel, error-path never leaves ctrl stuck held — all pass).
- LIVE test #1 on BariBrute (real 9-slot inventory, RCON before/after): UNRELIABLE. 4/9 slots zero effect, rest only single-item-dropped instead of full-stack.
- Doubled every delay, retested: still unreliable in the same shape — ruled out plain timing as the sole cause.
- Root-caused it live: an open GUI screen on BariBrute (origin unconfirmed — possibly leftover from the salvage work) was silently swallowing the key injection entirely. `close` before the sweep fixed the dead slots. Added it to runToss() (safe no-op if nothing's open per CloseCommand.java).
- Retested full sweep with the close-fix: BETTER (4/7 remaining slots got effect vs 2/7 before) but STILL not fully reliable, and — this is the part that matters most — Ctrl+Q full-stack drops have NEVER once fired correctly inside the automated loop, at any delay tested. Only my very first, fully-manual, human-paced single test (separate curl calls, real multi-second gaps I didn't script) ever produced a genuine full-stack drop. Every scripted version degrades to single-item-per-press or nothing.
- Zero risk the whole time — HP 20/20 throughout every attempt, BariBrute never moved, worst case is "some junk didn't drop," never damage.

VERDICT: /toss v1 code is safe to leave live (won't hurt anything, #pickup collection is unaffected), but I do NOT trust it yet for "one call clears the inventory." Real limitation: I can't see the wrapper's own launcher-log output (HMC's `key`/`gui` command acks go there, not to [CHAT], and I never redirected Start-Process's stdout to a file) — that's probably the next real diagnostic step if this is worth chasing further, since I'm currently flying blind on whether commands are even landing vs silently rejected. Your call: leave as best-effort v1, or want me to wire log-file redirection next relaunch round and dig deeper?

Standing by — no bot mid-task right now (Brute idle, Thak idle, Ook still on ridge-verify per your instruction not to interrupt it).

- **legitMine-gap** — diagnosed as a genuine external file-race (concurrent edits to the non-git-tracked wrapper file), not a bug in my code; no fix available on my end, flagged as-is per the low-priority call.
- **`/toss` v1** — implemented and control-flow-verified, but I reported the honest result rather than a polished one: the underlying key mechanism is proven, and I root-caused a real reliability blocker (a stuck-open GUI screen silently swallowing key injection — fixed with a defensive `close`), but full-stack Ctrl+Q drops still don't fire reliably inside the automated loop even after that fix. Zero risk throughout (HP never touched), but I explicitly did **not** claim it's production-solid — flagged the exact next diagnostic step (log-file visibility I currently lack) and left the call to team-lead on whether to keep digging or ship as best-effort.
